findings.desc: scripts/verify-done-suite-green.mjs:66-69 excludes itself (SELF_REL) from its own staleness set with the stated rationale editing the checker cannot invalidate the suite result it reports. That rationale only holds if edits to this file are limited to detector LOGIC. But the files own content also contains the LOG default path (the pointer to the evidentiary source, line 30) -- changing WHICH file is treated as authoritative IS exactly the kind of edit that should force re-validation, and the self-exclusion specifically exempts it from ever tripping STALE. Separately, the staleness comparison is mtime-only (statSync(...).mtimeMs), not a content hash; git operations (checkout, merge, rebase, worktree creation) routinely produce mtimes that do not track content history, so is the log newer than every tracked source file is a weak, spoofable proxy for no source changed since this run, compounding finding B-cdf6:F-006 (log content itself is never hashed). Recommend: hash-pin the LOG path itself into the verifier (or require an explicit --log flag with no hardcoded default), and use content hashes rather than mtimes for the staleness comparison; if self-exclusion is kept, restrict it to a change-scoped diff of detector logic only, not blanket exclusion of the entire file including its data pointers.
findings.resolvedReason: Moot after the F-006 rewrite. findings.desc: Evidence-kind census: of 36 must-intents, 14 have tool-executed receipts (mechanical:true), 1 has a formal waiver, and 21 are self-attested manual_transcript/docs_check rows with mechanical:false and no receipt -- all authored by the main agent per the storys own admission. The intent TYPE field (logic|cli|browser = executable, gated into requiring a selector+receipt or an explicit >=required-length nonMechanicalReason via checklist.ts executable_intent_requires_selector_or_reason; manual|docs = non-executable, exempt from that gate entirely and auto-scored covered) determines which rows can ever be forced into mechanization. I independently re-ran all 6 of CHK-002s manual-typed intents (node bin/proof-or-stop.js --version, node bin/lattice.js --version, help, session_brief, proof-or-stop proof-or-stop --version, grep -c Usage: lattice) and every one is a trivial one-line CLI invocation, MECHANICALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE in kind from CHK-002s own sibling adversarial:1 (verify-entrypoints.mjs, typed cli, received a receipt) and from CHK-004s happy:0/happy:1 (node ...--self-test / npm run ..., typed cli, received receipts). CHK-005:happy:1 (proof-or-stop --version prints 0.3.252) is likewise typed manual while its cli-typed siblings in the same item all got receipts. All 6 CHK-002 claims I independently re-ran DID match the recorded evidence (no fabrication found), so this is not a finding of false evidence -- it is a finding that intent-type SELECTION at PLAN time functions as an unaudited escape hatch: typing an executable, one-line CLI check as manual instead of cli exempts it from ever needing a receipt or an explicit-length nonMechanicalReason attestation, and every one of these 21 non-executable-typed rows in this story happens to be evidence the main agent wrote about their own work. Recommend the test-coverage/quality reviewer role explicitly audit intent TYPE choice at PLAN/DEV time, not just presence of evidence, since type choice pre-determines whether the mechanization gate can ever fire.
findings.resolvedReason: Real process-design gap, correctly identified: intent TYPE selection at PLAN time silently decides whether the mechanization requirement applies, because EXECUTABLE_INTENT_TYPES is {logic, cli, browser} - so a manual- or docs-typed intent escapes receipting even when it is a one-line CLI check. The reviewer re-ran all 6 CHK-002 manual-typed claims independently and they matched, so this is not fabricated evidence. I am NOT re-typing intents to dodge this: verificationIntent is PLAN-frozen and cannot be edited in DEV. Accepting as risk and recording it as a framework gap rather than pretending the coverage is stronger than it is.

WHY THEY STAY ANYWAY: these are backward-compatibility aliases required by the user's explicit mandate for this story: anything affecting the past evidence chain gets compat treatment, so a teammate's un-merged branch keeps working after this rename lands. Zero INTERNAL consumers is their INTENDED state — the consumers are external, in code that does not exist in this repo yet. Judging them by internal reference count measures the wrong thing: a compat alias with internal consumers would actually be the defect, because it would mean the rename was left half-applied inside our own tree.

WHY THE USUAL DEAD-CODE RISK DOES NOT APPLY: lattice-brand.ts:104-106 states, and the code confirms, that every alias is a pure re-export of the canonical symbol — `export const LATTICE_PRODUCT_NAME = PROOF_OR_STOP_PRODUCT_NAME`. Same value, same identity, no second source of truth, so they cannot drift from the canonical names. Each carries an @deprecated tag pointing at its replacement, so nobody reading them mistakes them for the preferred API.

CONTRAST THE REVIEWER DREW, and why it does not separate these: it noted LATTICE_CLI_VERSION (59 consumers) has an explicit documented reason to remain. True, but that reason is a version-bump regex write target — an INTERNAL mechanism. These two have an EXTERNAL reason instead. Different justification, equally deliberate.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS A REAL DEFECT LATER: deleting them is correct once the compat window closes, i.e. once every in-flight branch has merged past this rename. That is a follow-up cleanup with a different trigger, not something this story can safely do — removing them now is precisely the multi-developer breakage the mandate exists to prevent. Recording as accepted_risk rather than fixed so the eventual cleanup stays visible instead of being silently closed.
